[stop_reason: hop_cap_reached | hops used: 4/4] Analyst summary: **Investigation summary – “Exxon Mobil disruption reported around 29 Aug 2005”** --- ### 1. Companies that are structurally downstream of Exxon Mobil (2‑tier view) | Tier | Company (has filing?) | Business sector | |------|-----------------------|-----------------| | **Tier 1** (direct customers) | General Motors – *HAS a filing* (but none dated ≤ 30 Aug 2005) | Automotive | | | Jiangsu Lopal Tech – NO filing | Chemicals | | | Alfa SAB de CV – NO filing | Chemicals | | | Dongsung Chemical – NO filing | Chemicals | | | Volkswagen – NO filing | Automotive | | … (≈ 10 more Tier‑1 firms) | | | | **Tier 2** (customers of Tier‑1 or alternative suppliers) | Korea Electric Power – *HAS a filing* (20‑F filed 30 Jun 2005) | Electric utilities | | | BP – *HAS a filing* (20‑F filed 30 Jun 2005) | Oil & gas | | | Adient – HAS a filing (none ≤ 30 Aug 2005) | Automotive interiors | | | Romeo Power – HAS a filing (none ≤ 30 Aug 2005) | EV batteries | | | Dow – HAS a filing (none ≤ 30 Aug 2005) | Chemicals | | | Toyota Motor – *HAS a filing* (20‑F filed 24 Jun 2005) | Automotive | | | Ford Motor – *HAS a filing* (10‑K filed 10 Mar 2005) | Automotive | | … (≈ 40 more Tier‑2 firms) | | | Only the companies **highlighted in bold** have filings that were available for review and therefore could be examined for any mention of the August‑2005 Exxon Mobil event. --- ### 2. Evidence gathered | Company | Source(s) consulted | What the source says about a link to Exxon Mobil (or related risk) | |---------|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------| | **Korea Electric Power (KEPCO)** | • 20‑F filing dated 30 Jun 2005 (≈ 2 months before the event)
• Targeted corpus search (“Exxon Mobil”) within KEPCO documents | The filing discusses **fuel‑price exposure** (oil price spikes in May 2005) and notes that higher fuel costs “may have a material adverse effect on results of operations”. No explicit reference to the specific Exxon Mobil disruption, but the document shows KEPCO’s sensitivity to oil‑price volatility – a plausible downstream impact if Exxon Mobil’s supply chain were impaired. | | **BP** | • 20‑F filing dated 30 Jun 2005
• Targeted corpus search (“Exxon Mobil”) within BP documents | The filing contains a paragraph that references **≈ 200 lawsuits stemming from the 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill**, noting that “most of those suits named Exxon (now ExxonMobil) …”. This is a historical legal link, not a direct operational impact from the 2005 disruption. No mention of current supply‑chain or production issues tied to the August 2005 event. | | **Toyota Motor** | • 20‑F filing dated 24 Jun 2005 | The filing’s risk‑factor section lists “fuel shortages or interruptions in transportation systems” as a possible adverse factor, but there is **no specific mention of Exxon Mobil** or any disruption affecting its fuel supply. | | **Ford Motor** | • 10‑K filing dated 10 Mar 2005 | The filing similarly cites general risks (e.g., “fuel shortages”, “labor strikes”) without naming Exxon Mobil or describing a concrete impact from the August 2005 event. | | **General Motors** | • No filing covering the period ≤ 30 Aug 2005 (the earliest filing in the system is later) | Consequently, there is **no documentary evidence** that can be examined for any mention of an Exxon Mobil disruption. | *Companies without a filing (e.g., Jiangsu Lopal Tech, Alfa SAB, Volkswagen, Adient, Romeo Power, Dow, etc.) could not be checked with `get_supplier_info`. A corpus‑wide search was only performed for the two companies above; no other firm returned a relevant “Exxon Mobil” hit in the limited query set.* --- ### 3. What **could NOT** be confirmed | Company | Reason for lack of confirmation | |---------|---------------------------------| | All Tier‑1 firms (General Motors, Volkswagen, Jiangsu Lopal Tech, etc.) | No filing dated on or before 30 Aug 2005; therefore `get_supplier_info` returned nothing and no targeted corpus search was performed for them. | | Many Tier‑2 firms with filings (Adient, Romeo Power, Dow, etc.) | Their most recent filings are **after** the event date, so they contain no contemporaneous discussion of an August 2005 disruption. | | Any direct operational impact on downstream customers (e.g., loss of fuel supply, production stoppages) | None of the examined documents explicitly mention a disruption at Exxon Mobil in late‑August 2005, nor do they describe concrete knock‑on effects for the listed downstream companies. The only references found are historical (Exxon Valdez lawsuits) or generic risk‑factor language about fuel price volatility and supply interruptions. | | Companies that appear only in the “reachable but not enriched” list (e.g., Linde India, Mercedez‑Benz, etc.) | No enrichment data → no basis for targeted evidence; they remain **unverified**. | --- ### 4. Bottom‑line assessment * The structural supply‑chain map shows a large number of downstream automotive, chemicals and utilities firms that could theoretically be affected by an Exxon Mobil disruption. * However, the **only contemporaneous filings available (KEPCO, BP, Toyota, Ford)** do **not** contain any explicit statement linking those companies to the specific August 2005 event. The few mentions that do appear are either historical legal references (BP) or generic exposure to oil‑price swings (KEPCO). * For the majority of identified downstream firms—especially Tier‑1 automotive manufacturers and many Tier‑2 suppliers—**no documentary evidence** could be retrieved because filings covering the relevant period are absent. **Conclusion:** While a broad set of companies is structurally connected to Exxon Mobil, the limited public filings and corpus excerpts available up to 30 Aug 2005 do **not provide concrete confirmation** that any of these downstream firms experienced material disruption as a result of the reported August‑2005 incident at Exxon Mobil. The investigation therefore remains **incomplete** for most downstream entities; only generic risk exposures can be inferred from the evidence that was obtainable.
